## Analysis Summary

**Test image observations:**
- Very young soybean seedlings (first trifoliate leaf stage) that have completely collapsed and died
- Leaves are totally desiccated, brown, and crinkled/curled
- Plants have failed at or near the soil line
- Dark, moist soil — wet field conditions
- Healthy green plants visible in background (patchy distribution)

**Reference image comparison:**
- **Phytophthora** — Best match: top-left panel of reference showed identical dead/collapsed young seedlings in moist field soil. Phytophthora causes early-season damping off and seedling collapse in wet conditions.
- **Pythium** — Reference showed even younger (cotyledon stage) failing seedlings with water-soaked lesions; test image plants are older.
- **Rhizoctonia** — Reference showed reddish-brown sunken lesions at soil line on more established plants; not matching.
- **Fusarium** — Reference showed root/stem rot with scorching of upper leaves; not matching.
- **Anthracnose, Diaporthe, Charcoal Rot** — All showed mature plant/pod symptoms; not applicable.
- **SDS, Brown Stem Rot** — Showed interveinal necrosis on mature leaves; not matching.

**Key discriminating feature**: The complete and sudden collapse/death of young seedlings in moist soil conditions is characteristic of Phytophthora root and stem rot early-season damping off. The field context (dark moist soil, patchy death with healthy plants nearby) strongly supports this.
